**Note:** You can use this file as you 'working document' where you can try out various investigation ideas and keep notes about your findings. How you use and structure this file is up to you. It is recommended that you keep notes about what you are investigating and what you find as this will make the process of creating your presentation and report easier. Please note that you _do not_ need to submit this file as part of your group project.

Question: To what extent are students’ family socioeconomic status, parental education, and home learning resources associated with their mathematics performance in PISA 2025?


```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```


```{r load-lib, message = FALSE}
# Add any other libraries here
library(tidyverse)
library(learningtower)
library(haven)

```


```{r load-data}
# load your data 
student_math <- read_rds("data/student_math.rds")
# remove useless colomns
student_math_pro <- student_math %>%
  select(!general_family_support)%>%
  select(!home_ict_resources)
# mean_math_score
student_math_pro <- student_math_pro %>%
  mutate(
    mean_math_score = (
      math_score_pv1 +
      math_score_pv2 +
      math_score_pv3 +
      math_score_pv4 +
      math_score_pv5 +
      math_score_pv6 +
      math_score_pv7 +
      math_score_pv8 +
      math_score_pv9 +
      math_score_pv10
    ) / 10
  )
```

``` {r Tidy Data}
# students’ family socioeconomic status + math score
student_math_ses <- student_math_pro %>%
  select(student_id,
         family_socioeconomic_status,
         family_support,
         home_possessions_index,
         mean_math_score
  )

student_math_ses
```

``` {r}
# parental education + math score
student_math_education <- student_math_pro %>%
  select(student_id,
         highest_parental_education,
    parental_education_years,
    highest_parental_occupational_status,
    mean_math_score
  )

student_math_education
```

``` {r}
# studentinfo + math score
student_math_studentinfo <- student_math_pro %>%
  select(student_id,
         country_code,
         student_age,
         student_gender,
         mean_math_score
    )

student_math_studentinfo
```

``` {r}
# A better code which only shows the mean scores.
student_means <- student_math %>% 
  group_by(country_code) %>%
  summarise(
    math_mean1 = mean(math_score_pv1, na.rm = TRUE),
    n = n()
    ) 
student_means
```
